title: Check yourself: starting and joining threads

questions.stem: A checkout handler starts a thread that computes the customer's discount into a field, and on the next line reads that field to build the response. In every test run so far the response included the discount. What can production responses look like?

options.text: No response will lack the discount, since run() has already begun by the time start() returns
options.says: start() makes the thread runnable and returns; it doesn't wait for run() to begin

options.text: Some responses may lack the discount, since start() returns without waiting for run() to do anything
options.says: nothing orders the new thread against the caller's next line, so the field may still be unset

options.text: No response will lack the discount, since the test runs show the new thread winning that race in this code
options.says: the order seen on one machine is a property of that machine; pinned to one core the other order came up in about one run in seven

options.text: Some responses may lack the discount, since start() runs the new thread only after the caller's method returns
options.says: start() makes the thread runnable at once; the scheduler may run it before, during or after the caller's next line

origin.section: start() Doesn't Wait for the New Thread to Do Anything

questions.stem: A command-line tool's main() parses its arguments, calls Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> upload(file)) and returns. The upload takes about three seconds. What happens?

options.text: The JVM can exit before the upload is done, since returning from main cancels the threads main started
options.says: returning from main cancels nothing; the JVM exiting is what ends the upload

options.text: The upload completes and then the JVM exits, since the JVM waits for the threads main started
options.says: the JVM waits only for non-daemon threads, and a virtual thread is a daemon thread

options.text: The upload completes and then the JVM exits, since a running virtual thread keeps the JVM alive
options.says: virtual threads are daemon threads, so they don't keep the JVM alive

options.text: The JVM can exit before the upload is done, since virtual threads are daemon threads
options.says: a virtual thread is a daemon thread; once main returns and no non-daemon thread is left, the JVM exits

origin.section: start() Doesn't Wait for the New Thread to Do Anything

questions.stem: A loader thread fills a cache map and then sets a plain, non-volatile boolean loaded = true. A request thread waits with while (!loaded) { } and then reads the map. Nobody joins the loader, which finishes after 400 ms. What can happen to the request thread?

options.text: It may stay in the loop after the loader has finished, since nothing orders the loader's write before the request thread's reads
options.says: with no happens-before edge the JIT may read the field once and spin on that value forever

options.text: It may stay in the loop after the loader has finished, since its own loop keeps the loader from writing to the field it reads
options.says: reading a plain field blocks nobody; the loader's write happens, and what is missing is any rule that the reader will see it

options.text: It leaves the loop soon after the loader has finished, since a write to a boolean field is atomic
options.says: an atomic write is not a visible one; only a hand-over such as join(), isAlive() returning false, a volatile field or a latch makes it visible

options.text: It leaves the loop soon after the loader has finished, since a thread's writes are published to other threads when it terminates
options.says: termination makes the writes visible only to a thread that joins it or sees isAlive() return false

origin.section: Spot the Problem: A Done Flag Instead of join()

questions.stem: A shutdown hook computes a deadline 5 seconds ahead, runs some cleanup, then calls exporter.join(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS.toMillis(deadline - System.nanoTime())). The cleanup took 4,999.7 ms, and the exporter thread is stuck writing to a network share that is down. What does the hook do at the join?

options.text: It returns at once, since a timeout below one millisecond means no wait at all
options.says: the remaining 0.3 ms rounds down to join(0), and join(0) waits forever, by the javadoc

options.text: It waits for as long as the exporter runs, since the timeout it passes means no limit at all
options.says: 0.3 ms rounds down to 0 ms, and a timeout of 0 means to wait forever

options.text: It returns at once, since a join whose timeout has run out throws and the hook moves on
options.says: join(millis) returns nothing and throws nothing when its time runs out; only a negative timeout throws

options.text: It waits for as long as the exporter runs, since a timed join returns early only when the joined thread is interrupted
options.says: a timed join returns when its time is up whether or not the thread is interrupted; the problem here is the timeout of 0

origin.section: join(millis) Returns Without Saying Why, So Ask isAlive()
